title: Ambient Adaptive Spectral Accent Mapper and Console Component Contrast Synthesis
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: Our current theme token mappings are static across brand variants and do not account for ambient lighting or perceptual color shifts. This produces inconsistent contrast on interactive states (button press, table row hover, chart strokes) when customers use brand themes with highly saturated accents in dark mode. Goal: Design a deterministic, prescriptive pipeline — the Spectral Accent Mapper — that adapts brand accents into a set of console-safe accent tokens and component contrast deltas based on ambient-level heuristics and accessibility constraints. Deliverables: design token transformation rules, example token sets for 3 brand archetypes (neutral, saturated, pastel), component override rules for buttons/tables/charts, and an integration spec for engineering to generate runtime-mapped variants for Private/Dedicated/Hosted console themes.
acceptance_criteria: Token transformation function defined and documented: input (brand-primary hex + ambient-level) -> output token set (accent-1..accent-5, accent-muted)
Generated accent token sets for 3 canonical brand archetypes with visual QA pass (design review) and color contrast checks >= WCAG AA for primary interactive states at configured ambient levels
Component override guidelines documented and prototyped in Figma: primary/secondary/tertiary button states, table header/row separators, chart stroke and area fills
Engineering integration spec supplied with examples and unit test vectors; mapping function deterministic and reversible within tolerance thresholds
Rollout plan with canary in dark-mode-heavy orgs and telemetry hooks for contrast regressions
design_decisions: Use perceptual HCT-ish space for token delta calculations to preserve hue intent while adjusting chroma/lightness
Ambient levels represented as three buckets: low (dim), medium (desk), high (bright) — mapped to preflight multipliers for lightness shifts
Prefer contrast-preserving tints over naive desaturation for accents used in interactive states to keep brand recognition
Provide a minimal fallback palette (3 tones) for constrained environments (older browsers, limited color depth)
Expose explicit token names (accent.primary, accent.primary-pressed, accent.primary-muted) to avoid implicit overrides across components
implementation_notes: Prototype mapping implemented as pure function in design system repo (tools/color-mapper.js) with vectorized unit tests
Engineers will expose mapping as build-time token generation and as lightweight runtime fallback for Private console when runtime sensors (ambient) are present
Backwards compatibility: if brand theme pins exact tokens, mapping is skipped but a warning is emitted in the console to indicate potential contrast issues
Provide a variant-generation script that emits JSON token bundles and CSS variables for Hosted/Dedicated deployments
Quantify acceptable delta: ΔL* tolerance of ±3 and ΔC* clamp to prevent oversaturation in dark surfaces
testing_plan: Automated color-contrast checks for all generated tokens vs surface tokens using Lighthouse/A11y tooling
Manual visual QA in Figma prototypes across three brand archetypes and 4 surface elevations
Integration tests: render sample pages with mapped tokens and capture snapshots under simulated ambient levels
Performance test: ensure token generation runtime <50ms for on-the-fly mapping and bundle size impact <2KB gzipped per theme
rollout_plan: Phase 1: internal opt-in for design and SE teams to test with curated brand themes
Phase 2: canary roll for 5% of Hosted customers with dark-mode default and telemetry collection on contrast regressions
Phase 3: enable as recommended mapping in Console Theming UI with toggle for customers to opt out
Phase 4: full rollout with docs, migration guide, and automated fixes where possible
